subject: BrightCart search discovery — index sizing & rerank success criteria
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 05 Aug 2026 14:15:00 -0700
Subject: BrightCart search discovery — index sizing & rerank success criteria

Hi Priya —

Great speaking with you and Jose earlier. Quick recap from our discovery call and the concrete next steps we discussed so we have a clear PoC scope. Let me know if I missed anything.

Key pain points you shared:
- Production relevance drift: current top-10 is noisy for long-tail queries and promotions.
- Cost + latency tradeoff: need sub-300ms end-to-end response for search + rerank at peak traffic, while keeping hosting costs predictable.
- Operational friction: multiple silos (search infra, offline re-ranking) make experiments slow and rollout risky.

Current stack you described:
- Query layer: ElasticSearch 7.10 (document metadata + retrieval)
- Vector store: Faiss on a smaller offline cluster for embeddings lookups (batch offline updates)
- Rerank: a lightweight XGBoost model for pairwise scoring, occasionally an LLM-based rerank for key cases
- Metadata and user signals in Postgres / Redshift; ingestion cadence ~daily for cold docs, hourly for promoted items
- Estimated corpus: ~120M total docs; ~18M active (freshly updated) vectors; average doc vector dims ~1536

Success criteria for a Redwood-led PoC (what you called "go/no-go"):
- Relevance: 10-Recall (approx recall@10) improvement >= 15% over baseline, and MRR lift >= 0.12 on the priority query set.
- Latency: retrieval + rerank end-to-end p95 <= 300ms for 95% of requests during a 2-hour peak window. p50 target <= 120ms.
- Cost: incremental per-1M-query cost for the rerank path to be under $300 (target) at PoC scale.
- Ops: ability to run daily rollouts with Canary to 5% traffic and automatic fallback to current production path.

Operational patterns & constraints we noted:
- Peak QPS: 450 rps sustained with spikes to ~1.1k rps during promotions.
- Batch window: embeddings updates happen in hourly batches for promoted/fast-moving items, daily for the rest.
- Data residency: US-only for now (no EU data).
- Security: SOC2 attestation required; will need an evidence pack for the procurement team.

Immediate next steps (agreed):
1) You to send: a representative traffic sample (CSV), and the current search stack diagram (we discussed naming fields and the vector build frequency). Attachments: brightcart_traffic_sample.csv, search_stack_diagram.pdf.
2) Redwood to deliver: a short PoC plan + checklist and a scoped cost estimate for a 6-week PoC. Well propose a pilot infra layout (Hosted vs Dedicated) and recommended batching/quantization settings.
3) Success metric list + seed query set: you'll share the top 2k queries and three benchmark segments (home page, product detail, promotions).
4) Security questionnaire kickoff: we'll provide information on Redwood SOC2 artifacts and the initial security questionnaire by next Tue.

Proposed PoC timeline:
- Week 0: data handoff (you) + onboarding, sample ingestion
- Week 1-2: feature parity retrieval + candidate generation experiments (index sizing tests)
- Week 3-4: rerank integration & A/B evaluation
- Week 5-6: load testing, canary rollout, handoff to ops

If that aligns, Ill draft the PoC plan and a scoped invoice for the pilot compute.

Thanks again — enjoyed the pragmatic discussion.

Best,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: BrightCart search discovery — index sizing & rerank success criteria

Thanks Karthik — this looks right based on our call. A few clarifications/additions: 

- Corpus: 120M is total historical documents; our "active" set is closer to 22M after filtering for in-stock and promoted SKUs. Well send both full and active indexes in the sample.
- Rerank: we currently run XGBoost + feature-rich signals. LLM rerank is experimental for personalization — were interested in Redwoods hybrid suggestion (fast dense retrieval + lightweight rerank then LLM only for long-tail).
- Latency targets: for customer-facing search we need 95th percentile <= 350ms at peak; marketing is comfortable if p50 stays under 150ms. (We may relax p95 for purely internal analytics queries.)
- Cost target: model budget is flexible but procurement is asking for an estimate under $1,500 / 100k QPS-month for the PoC window (rough phrasing; will refine).

Attached the traffic sample and a simplified stack diagram. Note: the CSV contains anonymized user query, timestamp, and doc ids. Reach out if you need extra columns.

Next steps from our side: well upload the dataset and shared folder by EOD; Jose will coordinate the security contacts for questionnaire.

Appreciate the tight plan. Looking forward to the PoC doc.

—Priya
Head of Search, BrightCart

Perfect — thanks for the clarifications, Priya. Two quick follow-ups: 

1) Can you confirm the dimensionality of the active vectors (1536?) and whether youre currently using any quantization (int8/ivfpq) in Faiss for the offline store? That will affect memory + retrieval latency assumptions.
2) For the seed query set, is the top-2k anonymized file okay for the relevance eval, or do you prefer a smaller curated set + separate long-tail sample?

Ill start drafting the PoC doc and include two infrastructure options: Hosted (fast path, smaller setup) and Dedicated (predictable throughput + data isolation). Marissa, can you add a one-page checklist (redwood_poc_checklist.xlsx) covering security artifacts and milestone acceptance criteria?

If all good, well schedule a 30-min kickoff next Tue to run through the PoC plan end-to-end.

Karthik
